Around mid-October, reports emerged that Pakistan had shut key border crossings—Gabd-Rimdan and Taftan—used for trade with Iran. Iran and Pakistan share a border stretching more than 900 km. While Pakistan cited a security rationale, indications suggest the move resulted from American pressure to squeeze Iran. However, when LPG prices increased in Pakistan, it reopened the Gabd-Rimdan border crossing. Watch Bantirani Patro explain Pakistan's troubled borders, and how trade, investment and trust with all its bordering neighbours have withered.
